bottlenecks: detect_collisions is O(n^2) pairwise — no spatial partitioning (grid, kd-tree, quadtree) for 100+ agents; scales quadratically with swarm size
compute_all_avoidance_velocities is O(n^2) — every agent checks every other agent; no neighbor culling or locality-sensitive pruning
check_health iterates all agents in a single pass — O(n) heartbeat sweep with no sharding or hierarchical aggregation for large swarms
distribute_tasks is greedy O(n*m) — no batch optimization or parallel assignment for large task/agent counts
elect_leader is single-leader centralized — no hierarchical leader election (sub-swarms/regions) for 100+ agents; single point of coordination failure
_agents and _tasks are plain dicts — no indexed lookups for capability-based queries; _find_replacement scans all agents O(n) per task
predict_collisions is O(n^2) pairwise — no trajectory pruning or spatial hashing for collision prediction at scale
compute_velocity_obstacle uses safety_radius * 4 as cutoff but does not use prediction_horizon — predicted collisions may miss agents that will enter range within horizon
ORCA _find_optimal_velocity uses iterative projection (max 10 iterations) — no linear programming solver; may not find feasible velocity for dense swarms
DeadlockResolver._find_cycle_agents uses DFS with path copying — O(n^2) in dense wait-for graphs; no Tarjan's SCC for large swarms
TaskAllocator._hungarian is O(n^3) — no approximation or sampling for large-scale allocation (100+ agents/tasks)
SwarmCoordinator is fully centralized — all state in Python dicts; no distributed coordination or coordinator replication for 100+ agents
No communication range model — agents are assumed to communicate with all other agents regardless of distance; unrealistic for large fields
missing_algorithms: No flocking (Reynolds rules) — no separation/alignment/cohesion behaviors for group motion; agents move independently without group coherence
No Dynamic Window Approach (DWA) — velocity selection is proximity-based push-away only; no trajectory scoring over feasible velocity space with acceleration limits
No token-ring or blacklist-based coordination for narrow passages — no mechanism to serialize agents through bottlenecks or one-way passages
No market-based coordination beyond single-task auction — no currency/credit mechanism, no supply/demand matching, no task trading between agents
No coalition formation — agents cannot form sub-teams for tasks requiring multiple capabilities simultaneously; no merge/split of agent groups
No RRT*/PRM path planning — collision avoidance is reactive (push-away velocities) with no global or local path replanning around obstacles or other agents
No A*/Dijkstra pathfinding — agents have positions but no environment map or route planning; cannot navigate around static obstacles
No time-windowed task allocation — AllocationInstance has time_windows field but _greedy and _hungarian do not use it in cost computation or feasibility checks
No deadline-aware scheduling — AllocationInstance has deadlines field but allocation algorithms ignore deadlines; no EDF or priority-monotonic scheduling
No resource-constrained optimization — _check_resources is called only in _can_assign feasibility check, not in optimization objective; no multi-dimensional resource packing
No regret-based or online learning allocation — no mechanism to learn from past assignment outcomes to improve future allocations
No multi-objective optimization — only minimizes total cost; cannot optimize for cost, time, energy, fairness simultaneously
No dynamic reallocation — allocation is static; cannot reallocate when new tasks arrive or agents fail without full re-run
No rectangular Hungarian algorithm — falls back to greedy for non-square matrices; rectangular assignment is common (more tasks than agents)
No fairness metrics — no measure of allocation fairness; greedy can produce highly unbalanced allocations
No agent formation flying — no support for agents maintaining specific geometric formations during movement
No task decomposition — no mechanism to decompose complex tasks into subtasks for parallel execution
No communication constraints — no model of communication range or bandwidth limitations between agents
No heartbeat authentication — heartbeats are not authenticated; any process can send heartbeats for any agent
No metrics collection — no metrics on task completion time, agent utilization, swarm throughput; only logging is present
No simulation environment — no way to simulate agent movements, task execution, and failures in a controlled environment
No integration between modules — swarm, consensus, task_allocation, auction, contract_net, orca are independent; no top-level orchestrator integrating them
No common data model — Agent, Task, Position defined differently in each module; no shared abstractions
No configuration management — no centralized configuration for module parameters; each module has hardcoded defaults
No static obstacle avoidance — CollisionAvoidance only handles agent-agent collisions; no support for avoiding static obstacles (trees, buildings, rocks)
No 3D collision avoidance — only 2D positions supported; drones operate in 3D space and need altitude separation
No agent acceleration limits — no modeling of agent acceleration or deceleration limits; avoidance velocities applied instantaneously
No potential fields method — no attractive/repulsive force fields for goal-directed collision avoidance
No consensus integration into swarm — ByzantineConsensus exists but is not used by SwarmCoordinator for collective decision-making
No task allocation integration into swarm — TaskAllocator exists but SwarmCoordinator uses simple greedy matching instead
No path planning integration — SwarmCoordinator does not integrate with any path planner; agents assigned tasks but have no planned routes
benchmark_gaps: No performance benchmarks — no tests measuring wall-clock time or throughput at 50, 100, 500 agents
No stress tests — no tests for memory usage, assignment latency, or collision detection overhead as swarm grows
No scalability test for consensus — no test verifying PBFT quorum behavior with n=4,7,10 and f=1,2,3 nodes
No benchmark comparing greedy vs Hungarian — no test asserting Hungarian produces equal or lower total cost on random instances
No benchmark for collision avoidance quality — no test measuring collision rate (collisions per timestep) across swarm sizes
No fault-injection benchmarks — no tests measuring recovery time (detection → reassignment → completion) under various failure rates
No test for network partition tolerance — no test verifying consensus behavior when nodes are split into partitions
No test for Byzantine behavior detection — no test that a node sending conflicting votes is detected or excluded
No test for leader election convergence time — no test measuring rounds-to-election in bully algorithm
No test for task preemption correctness under contention — no test verifying priority inversion is avoided when high-priority tasks preempt
No integration test spanning all modules — no test that registers agents, assigns tasks, moves agents, detects collisions, and handles failures in one scenario
No test for collision avoidance with moving agents — all collision tests use static positions; no test with velocity-based prediction
No test for consensus with equivocating nodes — no test that a Byzantine node sending different values to different peers is handled
No benchmark for ORCA vs repulsive force — no test comparing collision-free guarantees and computational cost
No benchmark for auction vs greedy allocation — no test comparing solution quality and convergence time
No benchmark for contract net vs centralized allocation — no test comparing scalability and task completion rate
No test for flocking behavior — no test verifying separation/alignment/cohesion produce coherent group motion
No test for DWA trajectory quality — no test verifying dynamic window produces smooth, feasible trajectories
No test for token-ring bottleneck serialization — no test verifying agents pass through narrow passages without collision
No test for coalition formation — no test verifying agents form optimal sub-teams for multi-capability tasks
No test for 3D collision avoidance — no test verifying altitude separation for aerial agents
No test for static obstacle avoidance — no test verifying agents navigate around trees, buildings, rocks
No test for path planning integration — no test verifying agents follow planned routes to task locations
No test for dynamic reallocation — no test verifying tasks are reallocated when agents fail mid-execution
No test for online allocation — no test verifying competitive ratio for streaming task arrivals
